CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2

the plan, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  TASK ORDER AMENDMENT WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING FOR ADDITIONAL
  ENGINEERING, CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT, AND INSPECTION SERVICES
  FOR THE PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT DAPPLEGRAY SCHOOL PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council provide direction regarding the previously
  approved “No Right Turn on Red” restriction, including whether to maintain the
  restriction as approved, modify it (such as limiting it to peak hours), or rescind it.

Public Works Manager Graham provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), and
introduced the City’s Deputy Traffic Engineer, Wes Pringle who provided a presentation
including the analysis, traffic counts, video observations, alternative improvements and his
recommendation.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that it was a unanimous decision at the last
discussion, and that nothing presented has shifted her opinion on this item, with the top goal
being public safety. She also suggested not having time restrictions for the no-right-turn.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ appreciated the recommended time restrictions from the
City Engineer.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER inquired if equestrians were observed crossing the street
and noted that that corner has been a concern brought to the Equestrian Committee in the
past. She also noted that the Traffic & Safety Committee considered the new Nature Center
that will add to pedestrian use of the intersection in the future.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from Lynn Yes in favor of the recommendation, and Jim Deutsch
in opposition of the recommendation.

Discussion ensued about the possibility and timing of a leading pedestrian interval.

Assistant City Attorney McEwen explained that the Council’s consideration is whether to
continue, modify, or rescind a previously approved safety enhancement at the intersection,
which had been adopted in December based on documented concerns regarding its alignment

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 24, 2026
 and supporting data, including prior analyses and photographic evidence. He emphasized that
the Council’s primary objective should be public safety rather than determining whether the
intersection meets the legal definition of a “dangerous condition” under the Government Code.
He noted that the Council has discretion to proceed with the improvement, modify it, take no
action, or rescind it entirely. He further advised that maintaining the safety enhancement could
help mitigate potential liability risks to the City in the event of an accident, while rescinding it
could increase exposure to such risk, though he stopped short of characterizing the situation
as a legally defined dangerous condition.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER clarified that this intersection issue has been under
consideration for several years, not just recently, explaining that during her approximately six
years on the Traffic and Safety Committee, the matter was raised multiple times by different
individuals with varying concerns. She noted the issue has also been reviewed from an
equestrian perspective when it was brought before the Equestrian Committee, and
emphasized that this has been an ongoing effort involving repeated evaluation, including signal
timing considerations, rather than a sudden or new initiative, and expressed appreciation for
the recent work done on the matter.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ asked about the hours of an existing “no right turn” restriction
at Crenshaw Boulevard and Palos Verdes Drive North, and expressed concern that having
different rules at nearby intersections could confuse drivers and reduce the effectiveness of
signage due to overuse. Other Council Members responded that, while consistency is
generally desirable, the intersections in question have different physical constraints and safety
considerations, making uniform rules impractical. They noted that the specific intersection
discussed presents greater safety challenges due to its geometry and nearby pedestrian
activity, justifying a different approach despite concerns about signage and varying time
restrictions.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  UPHOLD THE CITY COUNCIL’S PREVIOUSLY APPROVED “NO RIGHT
  TURN ON RED” RESTRICTION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  NOES:  Schmitz
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ noted that she wanted to ask about maintaining the
restriction with the same 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. weekday hours but acknowledged support
from others for treating the intersection differently due to its unique physical constraints.
There was general agreement on the need to act proactively to prevent accidents, along
with a suggestion for staff to evaluate additional measures such as a leading pedestrian
interval to improve safety.
